measurement: source maps source map ingest + attribution (shipped binary, release build)
protocol: bench-spec.md §2 — 3 runs per input, median reported; peak RSS sampled at 100 ms by harness/run-bench.ps1

scaling_verdict.sme: 5x sources (10k -> 50k) costs 30.6x time and 2.3x memory: superlinear
scaling_verdict.nopeat: 5x sources costs 4.5x time (46 -> 209 ms) and roughly linear memory: 67 MB for a 36.5 MB map
scaling_verdict.conclusion: the win mechanism is the one predicted in docs/en/evidence.md §3: flat Vec<Mapping> with no per-mapping allocation plus a single-pass attribution, not 'Rust parses faster'. A Rust parser over the same data is only ~1.6x faster than @babel/parser; the 400x-2690x gaps come from removing the allocation and the nested walk.

targets.B5: ≤ 1 s for a 50 MB / 10k-source map: met at 46 ms median (10k) and 209 ms (50k, 36.5 MB)

open: attributed bytes are counted per source path; the join to stats modules (the fusion) is not yet measured, so the end-to-end fusion number stays unverified
